name: Parker House Rolls (Unfermented)
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: large teaspoonfuls of baking powder
ingredients.originalText: three large teaspoonfuls of baking powder

instructions.text: Stir into a quart of sifted flour three large teaspoonfuls of baking powder, a tablespoonful of cold butter, a teaspoonful of salt and one of sugar, and a well-beaten egg
Rub all well into the flour
Pour in a pint of cold milk and mix up quickly into a smooth dough
Roll it out less than half an inch thick
Spread soft butter over the top of each
Fold one-half over the other by doubling it
Lay them a little apart on greased tins
Set them immediately in a pretty hot oven
Rub over the tops with sweet milk before putting in the oven to give them a glaze

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stir into a quart of sifted flour three large teaspoonfuls of baking powder, a tablespoonful of cold butter, a teaspoonful of salt and one of sugar, and a well-beaten egg
2. Rub all well into the flour
3. Pour in a pint of cold milk and mix up quickly into a smooth dough
4. Roll it out less than half an inch thick
5. Cut with a large biscuit-cutter
6. Spread soft butter over the top of each
7. Fold one-half over the other by doubling it
8. Lay them a little apart on greased tins
9. Set them immediately in a pretty hot oven
10. Rub over the tops with sweet milk before putting in the oven to give them a glaze
